34.0.0.en: 1 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel, prophesy, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD unto the shepherds; Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks? 3 Ye eat the fat, and ye clothe you with the wool, ye kill them that are fed: but ye feed not the flock. 4 The diseased have ye not strengthened, neither have ye healed that which was sick, neither have ye bound up that which was broken, neither have ye brought again that which was driven away, neither have ye sought that which was lost; but with force and with cruelty have ye ruled them. 5 And they were scattered, because there is no shepherd: and they became meat to all the beasts of the field, when they were scattered. 6 My sheep wandered through all the mountains, and upon every high hill: yea, my flock was scattered upon all the face of the earth, and none did search or seek after them. 7 Therefore, ye shepherds, hear the word of the LORD; 8 As I live, saith the Lord GOD, surely because my flock became a prey, and my flock became meat to every beast of the field, because there was no shepherd, neither did my shepherds search for my flock, but the shepherds fed themselves, and fed not my flock; 9 Therefore, O ye shepherds, hear the word of the LORD; 10 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against the shepherds; and I will require my flock at their hand, and cause them to cease from feeding the flock; neither shall the shepherds feed themselves any more; for I will deliver my flock from their mouth, that they may not be meat for them."

34.0.1.en: "Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves.

34.0.2.en: Should not the shepherds feed the flocks?!

34.0.3.en: Ye eat the fat, and ye clothe you with the wool, ye kill them that are fed: but ye feed not the flock.

34.1.0.en: The diseased have ye not strengthened, neither have ye healed that which was sick, neither have ye bound up that which was broken, neither have ye brought again that which was driven away, neither have ye sought that which was lost; but with force and with cruelty have ye ruled them" [2-4]. When the heart of the shepherd turns away from the people of God to himself, he tends his own interests; he works for the sake of his own honor or possessions or bodily comfort, and so on... instead of caring for their needs and interests. He does not care for the sick, or the wounded, or the broken, or the driven away, or the lost, but cares for his selfishness. Such a one is not counted a shepherd but a hireling, who seeks the wage and not sonship; and sometimes he is counted a thief who steals the flock instead of guarding and supporting it.

34.1.1.en: *There are hirelings who work in the Church, of whom the Apostle Paul says: "For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's" (Phil 2:21).

34.1.2.en: What does "seek their own" mean? That they do not love Christ freely. They do not seek the things that are God's but seek temporal benefits; they gape for gain and are fond of seeking honor from men. Whenever any overseer desires such things and serves God in order to obtain them, then whoever this man may be, he is counted a hireling and cannot count himself among the sons, because of such men the Lord also said: "Verily I say unto you, They have their reward" (Mt 6:5)...

34.1.3.en: There are hirelings among us also, but the Lord alone separates them; He who knows the hearts separates them, though we are sometimes able to know them, for the Lord did not speak in vain in His discourse about the wolves: "Ye shall know them by their fruits" (Mt 6:17).

34.2.0.en: St. Augustine The shepherd's love of himself deprives him of the tender fatherhood that is gentle with the weak, and turns him not only into a hireling but into a violent tyrant, who loses his fatherhood and opens the door to tyranny. This violence drives the people to be scattered, so that they become a prey to all the beasts of the field [5], for they wander "through all the mountains, and upon every high hill, and upon all the face of the earth" [6].

34.2.1.en: Man becomes a prey to every kind of demon that devours the sheep of God because of the neglect of the shepherds and their preoccupation with themselves. Then the flock walks without aim or shelter, moving from mountain to mountain, from hill to hill, and from place to place, without discernment, wisdom or knowledge. The demons play with it, handing it over from one to another until it is utterly crushed.

34.3.0.en: "Behold, I am against the shepherds; and I will require my flock at their hand" [10].

34.3.1.en: Father Caesarius, bishop of Arles, says:

34.3.2.en: [Since the Lord has appointed us to steer the ship of His Church, may we, with His help and by the guidance of the two Testaments, govern the ship of His Church so that it may not turn aside to the right or to the left through our neglect, but may remain effortlessly in the straight course of life amid the great perils of this world. And just as no ship can gain earthly profits without hardships, so the ship of the Church cannot enjoy the gains and the joy of eternal things without many hardships].

34.3.3.en: The Lord cries out, saying: "Ye shepherds... my flock became a prey" [7-8], laying the responsibility upon them, since they became the means of crushing and destroying souls instead of being a refuge and a shelter for them from the ravening wolves.

34.3.4.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic wrote to Bishop Dracontium laying upon him the pastoral responsibility, saying to him: [Before you received the grace of the episcopate no one knew you, but you have become the one from whom the people expect to be given food, that is, the teachings of the Holy Scriptures. When they expect that and suffer hunger while you alone are filled, our Lord Jesus Christ will come and you will stand before Him; what defense will you offer when He finds His flock hungry?].

34.3.5.en: Sometimes it does not stop at their drinking the sweet waters alone or devouring spiritual food without their people; rather, what is more bitter is that in their selfishness they sometimes keep the deep waters for themselves, drinking from them, and do not leave even the shallow waters to their people, but foul them with their feet and offer them full of mud:

34.3.6.en: "Seemeth it a small thing unto you to have eaten up the good pasture, but ye must tread down with your feet the residue of your pastures? and to have drunk of the deep waters, but ye must foul the residue with your feet? And as for my flock, they eat that which ye have trodden with your feet; and they drink that which ye have fouled with your feet" [18-19]. St. Jerome sees that it is the muddy feet of the heretics that trouble the clear waters and corrupt the faith of the flock.

34.4.0.en: 11 For thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out. 12 As a shepherd seeketh out his flock in the day that he is among his sheep that are scattered; so will I seek out my sheep, and will deliver them out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day. 13 And I will bring them out from the people, and gather them from the countries, and will bring them to their own land, and feed them upon the mountains of Israel by the rivers, and in all the inhabited places of the country. 14 I will feed them in a good pasture, and upon the high mountains of Israel shall their fold be: there shall they lie in a good fold, and in a fat pasture shall they feed upon the mountains of Israel. 15 I will feed my flock, and I will cause them to lie down, saith the Lord GOD. 16 I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick: but I will destroy the fat and the strong; I will feed them with judgment. 17 And as for you, O my flock, thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I judge between cattle and cattle, between the rams and the he goats. 18 Seemeth it a small thing unto you to have eaten up the good pasture, but ye must tread down with your feet the residue of your pastures? and to have drunk of the deep waters, but ye must foul the residue with your feet? 19 And as for my flock, they eat that which ye have trodden with your feet; and they drink that which ye have fouled with your feet. 20 "Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD unto them; Behold, I, even I, will judge between the fat cattle and between the lean cattle. 21 Because ye have thrust with side and with shoulder, and pushed all the diseased with your horns, till ye have scattered them abroad; 22 Therefore will I save my flock, and they shall no more be a prey; and I will judge between cattle and cattle."

34.4.1.en: "Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out" [11]. Nothing is more precious to God than the human soul, which He brought into being in His image and likeness. If He has delivered His people into the hands of shepherds, it is only to honor humanity itself, that it may share with God, in His name and by His power, in the shepherding of souls; but God keeps this divine work for Himself, taking pride in it, saying: "Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out."

34.4.2.en: In His shepherding of His flock He does not tolerate the selfishness of the shepherds whom He appointed to serve His children, and so He stands Himself against them, counting every neglect or fault in shepherding as aimed at Him personally. He reassures every soul that the shepherds have exploited or neglected, saying: "Behold, I am against the shepherds; and I will require my flock at their hand, and cause them to cease from feeding the flock; neither shall the shepherds feed themselves any more; for I will deliver my flock from their mouth, that they may not be meat for them" [10]. He stands against them and takes over the shepherding Himself! He delights to call Himself "Shepherd," repeating the words "my flock" 14 times in this chapter, affirming that they are His people, for when He says "my people" they are His; He delivers them from the evil shepherds as He delivers them from the enemy outside, and takes their life into His own hands.

34.5.0.en: If the shepherds have preyed upon the flock, the Great Shepherd takes over His flock to judge for the weak flock against the violent shepherds: "Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD unto them; Behold, I, even I, will judge between the fat cattle (the tyrannical shepherd) and between the lean cattle (the poor flock)... Therefore will I save my flock, and they shall no more be a prey; and I will judge between cattle and cattle" [20-22]. All are equal before Me, shepherds and flock; I judge them all and judge between them, between cattle and cattle!

34.5.1.en: Thus the successful servant is the one who always lifts his eyes to the coming of the Great Shepherd, who will judge all without distinction. He does not show partiality nor care for honors; on the contrary, the one to whom more is given will be judged more and be required of more! The faithful servant is also the one who is always hidden in the Good Shepherd, so that he serves only through the one Shepherd, and works only by Him according to His divine mind. In this the servant is not puffed up against those he serves, nor does he think himself better than his brethren.

34.6.s.en: 3. The rise of a new shepherding:

34.6.0.en: 23 "And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd. 24 And I the LORD will be their God, and my servant David a prince among them; I the LORD have spoken it. 25 And I will make with them a covenant of peace, and will cause the evil beasts to cease out of the land: and they shall dwell safely in the wilderness, and sleep in the woods. 26 And I will make them and the places round about my hill a blessing; and I will cause the shower to come down in his season; there shall be showers of blessing. 27 And the tree of the field shall yield her fruit, and the earth shall yield her increase, and they shall be safe in their land, and shall know that I am the LORD, when I have broken the bands of their yoke, and delivered them out of the hand of those that served themselves of them. 28 And they shall no more be a prey to the heathen, neither shall the beast of the land devour them; but they shall dwell safely, and none shall make them afraid. 29 And I will raise up for them a plant of renown, and they shall be no more consumed with hunger in the land, neither bear the shame of the heathen any more. 30 Thus shall they know that I the LORD their God am with them, and that they, even the house of Israel, are my people, saith the Lord GOD. 31 And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your God, saith the Lord GOD."

34.6.1.en: Having spoken of God's care for mankind, he proclaimed the summit of this shepherding through "the Lord Christ," the true spiritual King, the Son of David, saying: "And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd" [23]. Without doubt "my servant David" does not mean the resurrection of King David from the dead to reign anew, but the appearing of the Lord Christ, the Son of God who became a servant, to reign over us through His love and humility.

34.6.2.en: On this St. John Chrysostom says: [As for Ezekiel and the other prophets, their speaking of David's coming and rising again does not mean that he is the one who died]. And Origen says: [It is not the patriarch (father) David who rises and rules the saints, but Christ]. St. Augustine also says: [Ezekiel speaks prophetically in the person of God the Father, telling beforehand about the Lord Christ in a prophetic way as "David," who took the form of a servant and became man, He who is the Son of God].

34.6.3.en: He speaks of this Good Shepherd, the Messiah the Savior, as one who:

34.7.0.en: a. Makes a covenant with mankind [25], which He writes not on tablets of stone but engraves in blood upon His holy body with divine love, so that He brings us into His bowels and we receive Him as an eternal Bridegroom.

34.7.1.en: b. Causes the evil beasts to cease out of the land, so that they dwell safely in the wilderness and sleep in the woods [25]. What are these evil beasts that He causes to cease out of the land if not the works of the old man, full of violence, which are removed from the land of our body so that we live in peace and safety?

34.7.2.en: Perhaps by the evil beasts He meant the Gentiles, who were like ravening beasts, which receive the faith and turn from their beastly nature to live with a new spirit and a new nature.

34.8.0.en: c. Sends down the shower in its season upon the hill about Him [26], which is the descent of the Lord Christ Himself from heaven, refreshing the soul and quenching the fire of its evils.

34.9.0.en: d. Gives the tree of the field, which is the Church, its fruit, and the earth yields her increase, so that safety comes upon the land [27]. He plants the tree of the New Covenant in His holy body, and it bears much fruit. He plants us in Him, so that our nature is blessed in Him and the land of our body is in constant safety.

34.9.1.en: e. Breaks the bands of their yoke and delivers them out of the hand of those that served themselves of them [27]. On the Cross He tears up the handwriting that was against us and frees us from the bondage of Satan, who had dominion over us. As the Apostle says: "Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross; and having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it" (Col 2:14-15). Therefore the prophet Ezekiel goes on to affirm, in the words of the Lord Himself: "And they shall no more be a prey to the heathen, neither shall the beast of the land devour them; but they shall dwell safely, and none shall make them afraid" [28]; that is, they will not become the prey of the demons, nor will the beast of the passions of the body (the earth) devour them, but they will be filled with the power of the Holy Spirit, the Giver of comfort and victory.

34.10.0.en: f. His work does not stop at breaking the yoke of the bondage of evil and driving out the beastly nature, but He offers the positive side: "I will raise up for them a plant of renown" [29]. He removes the old nature and gives the new nature, which is in His image, to work for man's being satisfied with Him personally.

34.11.0.en: g. What the Lord prides Himself upon is that He makes them "His people," and He is their God dwelling in their midst and united with them... "Thus shall they know that I the LORD their God am with them, and that they, even the house of Israel, are my people, saith the Lord GOD. And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your God, saith the Lord GOD" [30-31]. This is the conclusion of all His gifts: He comes forth as God to them, and they are His flock, His people; He takes pride in them and they take pride in Him. Therefore St. John the Beloved heard a description of heaven or eternal life thus: "Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God" (Rev 21:3).

34.11.2.en: *How wonderful You are, my Lord, in Your shepherding of me!

34.11.3.en: You threaten every selfish shepherd who seeks his own at the expense of Your flock!

34.11.4.en: You Yourself judge between the violent shepherds and the crushed flock!

34.11.5.en: *You came to our earth as a good Shepherd, You laid down Yourself for me and for every man!

34.11.6.en: You opened Your heavens to us as a satisfying pasture!

34.11.7.en: You surrounded us with Your Holy Spirit as a dew that softens our hearts.

34.11.8.en: You gave us the fruit of the Spirit in our depths!

34.11.9.en: *How sweet are Your words! And how mighty!

34.11.11.en: "Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out...

34.11.12.en: I will feed them in a good pasture...

34.11.13.en: I will feed my flock, and I will cause them to lie down...

34.11.14.en: I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick: but I will destroy the fat and the strong; I will feed them with judgment."
